About me

Who I am

I combine data engineering, artificial intelligence and full-stack development to turn raw data into products that people can use.

I'm in my final year of the Data Engineering program at ENSA Al Hoceima. My projects cover the whole chain, from collecting data out of APIs, websites and live GPS streams to processing it in real time or in batch, training models, and serving results through APIs and dashboards. Most of my larger projects were built in teams.

Data engineering

Batch and real-time pipelines with Spark, Kafka, Flink and Airflow, from raw data to clean, reliable tables.

AI & machine learning

Deep learning models, LLM applications, RAG systems and AI agents built with LangChain and LangGraph.

Analytics & BI

Data warehouses, star schemas and dashboards in Power BI, Grafana and Streamlit that help teams decide.

Full-stack development

Web applications with Spring Boot, FastAPI, React and Angular, from secure APIs to user interfaces.

    Capgemini Engineering

    AI Intern · Chatbot that designs mechanical parts

    Morocco

    An AI chatbot that takes a written description of a mechanical part, for example “a 40 mm flange with 4 holes”, and automatically generates its 3D design in CATIA.

  2. May – Jul 2026
    P

    PortNet

    Analytics & Data Science Intern · Supply chain optimization

    Morocco

    A model that predicts how long cargo stays at the port terminal, to reduce congestion and storage costs.

    ~490Kbills of lading
    1.2 daysMAE on 2024 test data
    0.78R² score
    8+models compared
    • Scoping & data pipeline. Led the analytics module end to end: gathered needs with operations teams, framed terminal congestion and storage costs as a dwell-time prediction problem, and built the full pipeline on about 490,000 real bills of lading (2020–2024), with leakage-free cleaning and feature engineering in Python (pandas) and SQL.
    • Statistical analysis & modeling. Ran exploratory and statistical analysis (correlation and significance tests) to find the main drivers of dwell time: importer history, cargo category, check-in delay and seasonality. Built and tuned 8+ modeling approaches (CatBoost, LightGBM, neural networks, stacking) with time-based validation, after finding and fixing a data-leakage bug that was distorting results.
    • Deployment & business reporting. Deployed the final CatBoost model in a Streamlit prediction app and dashboard, and presented charts and recommendations to the operations teams.

Project 01Real-time Big Data · MLTeam project · 2025–2026

TaaSim Casablanca

A real-time platform for taxis in Casablanca that matches riders with free taxis, tracks supply and demand in every district, and forecasts demand.

What I built

  1. 1Three Flink streaming jobs clean GPS data, compute supply and demand per district every 30 seconds, and match trips to taxis
  2. 2Spark MLlib forecasts demand from time and weather features
  3. 3A MinIO data lake and Cassandra store the data, served through a secured FastAPI and live Grafana maps

Results

~1.2 sto match a rider
~120 msper prediction
~12 srecovery, no data loss

Built with

Project 02ETL · RecommendationTeam project

Job Intelligent

A platform that collects data and AI job offers in Morocco every day and recommends the best matches for a candidate's CV.

What I built

  1. 1A daily Airflow pipeline scrapes LinkedIn with Selenium and calls the France Travail API
  2. 2PostgreSQL stores the data in Bronze, Silver and Gold layers: raw, cleaned and deduplicated
  3. 3TF-IDF matching ranks offers for an uploaded CV, served by FastAPI with JWT and a React app

Results

2job sources merged
Dailyautomatic refresh
3data quality layers

Project 04Big Data · Batch processingTeam project

Procurement Big Data Pipeline

An automated system that decides what to reorder from each supplier, every day, from over 1.5 million orders.

What I built

  1. 1Raw orders are stored on HDFS with a Hive Metastore, following a Lambda architecture
  2. 2Python and SQL logic computes net demand and respects supplier minimum quantities and pack sizes
  3. 3PostgreSQL was benchmarked against Trino: about 90 seconds instead of 5 minutes

Results

1.5M+orders per day
~80 MBper daily batch
~3.5 minfull daily cycle
